cheat_sheet.title: JavaScript, React and React Native Foundations — Structural Cheat Sheet
cheat_sheet.introduction: This sheet turns JavaScript, React and React Native Foundations into visible relationships. It is a reference for planning, tracing, debugging, and explaining—not a list to memorize.
cheat_sheet.why_it_matters: The level contributes directly to a React Native mobile application. Each concept helps the learner move from an ambiguous task to a contract, a representation, a verified transition, and an explainable result.

mental_model.summary: Represent the work as component trees, navigation graphs, event flows, and asynchronous timelines before translating it into implementation details.
reasoning_cycle: Model variables, state, constraints, and relationships

input_questions: What may be absent or malformed?
output_questions: What shape and state are promised?

core_concepts.rule: External text and device values require explicit type, absence, and range checks before application logic uses them.

core_concepts.title: Functions, arrays, and immutable updates
core_concepts.rule: Pure functions and non-mutating collection operations make state transitions predictable and testable.

core_concepts.title: Components and native render trees
core_concepts.rule: A React Native component maps props and state to native-view descriptions organized as a tree.

core_concepts.title: Props and one-way information flow
core_concepts.rule: Parents pass read-only inputs downward; children communicate events upward through explicit callback contracts.

core_concepts.title: State and event transitions
core_concepts.rule: State records information that affects rendering, and events produce discrete transitions from one valid snapshot to another.

core_concepts.title: Core components and platform differences
core_concepts.rule: Use portable primitives by default and isolate platform-specific behavior behind narrow, tested boundaries.

core_concepts.title: Styles, flex layout, and density
core_concepts.rule: Mobile layout uses flex constraints and logical units so content adapts to screen size, density, and text scale.

core_concepts.title: Project structure and debugging evidence
core_concepts.rule: Separate features, shared components, and services; use logs, inspector state, and minimal reproduction to locate failures.

common_mistakes: Starting with syntax before defining the input-output contract.
Combining current state and a candidate update so rejection cannot be safe.
Treating an observed normal result as proof for every boundary.
Choosing a structure because it is familiar rather than because its operations match the constraints.
Ignoring empty, missing, duplicate, maximum-size, repeated, or out-of-order cases.
Hiding failures instead of representing loading, empty, rejected, and error states explicitly.
Optimizing before measuring the actual bottleneck or risk.
Explaining what the implementation does without explaining why its invariant proves correctness.

Is the boundary inclusive or exclusive?
Can an invalid or repeated event mutate valid state?
Are asynchronous or external results stale, missing, or out of order?
Does the representation match the operation mix and constraints?
Did the repair pass the original failure and nearby regression cases?

lessons.title: JavaScript values and mobile input
lessons.goal: Model, apply, trace, and defend JavaScript values and mobile input within a native-feeling cross-platform experience.
lessons.learning_objective: Given a normal, boundary, or invalid case, the learner will use JavaScript values and mobile input to produce a valid result and explain the invariant or constraint that makes the result correct.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: JavaScript values and mobile input is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. External text and device values require explicit type, absence, and range checks before application logic uses them.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For JavaScript values and mobile input, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

content_blocks.title: See the system before the syntax
content_blocks.body: Use component trees, navigation graphs, event flows, and asynchronous timelines. Draw the boundary, label inputs and outputs, then trace one transition at a time.

inputs: The data or event that activates JavaScript values and mobile input
outputs: A value, decision, or visible state matching the contract
A preserved or deliberately updated next state
Evidence explaining acceptance or rejection

variables_and_state.name: candidate_input
variables_and_state.role: The untrusted or unverified incoming value

variables_and_state.name: current_state
variables_and_state.role: The last state known to satisfy all invariants

variables_and_state.name: constraint_result
variables_and_state.role: The explicit validation outcome

variables_and_state.name: next_state
variables_and_state.role: A proposed state computed without corrupting current_state

constraints: Inputs must match the declared shape and permitted boundary.
A rejected input must not corrupt the previous valid state.
The output must be representable by the current application workflow.
Every external or user-provided value is validated before use.
invariants: The governing relationship remains true: External text and device values require explicit type, absence, and range checks before application logic uses them.
At most one documented commit occurs for one accepted transition.
Invalid input leaves the last valid state unchanged.
step_by_step_reasoning: Restate the problem as a testable input-output contract.
List state variables and separate current state from a candidate update.
Write constraints as predicates with visible boundary choices.
Apply the structural rule for JavaScript values and mobile input.
Trace the normal case one transition at a time.
Trace an exact boundary and one invalid case.
Compare observed output and preserved invariants with the contract.
Record the first divergent state if the check fails.

worked_examples.scenario: A learner applies JavaScript values and mobile input while building a native-feeling cross-platform experience.

reasoning: Name the observable output before choosing an operation.
Represent only the state and relationships needed for that output.
External text and device values require explicit type, absence, and range checks before application logic uses them.
Trace the transition and compare the result with the contract.
worked_examples.output: A valid state transition with the promised result and recorded evidence.

worked_examples.title: Boundary case: valid at the limit
worked_examples.scenario: The input is exactly at the smallest or largest documented valid boundary.
worked_examples.input: A boundary value explicitly included by the constraint.
reasoning: Write the inclusive or exclusive boundary symbolically.
Evaluate the predicate before changing state.
Apply the same rule used for ordinary valid input.
Verify that the output remains representable and accessible.
worked_examples.output: The boundary case is accepted once and produces a valid output without special hidden state.

worked_examples.title: Rejected case: preserve the invariant
worked_examples.scenario: An input violates one required relationship or arrives in an unsupported state.
worked_examples.input: An out-of-contract value paired with a previously valid state.
reasoning: Identify the failed constraint and stop before commit.
Keep the previous valid state unchanged.
Return a specific, non-sensitive explanation or recovery path.
Record the case as evidence for a regression check.
worked_examples.output: A controlled rejection, preserved prior state, and actionable feedback.

common_mistakes: Beginning implementation before defining the required output.
Changing state before the input or transition has been validated.
Memorizing the label 'JavaScript values and mobile input' without applying its governing relationship.
Testing only one convenient normal case and assuming boundaries behave identically.
edge_cases: The smallest valid input or empty valid structure, when allowed.
The largest documented input, count, depth, size, or duration.
A duplicate, repeated event, retry, or already-completed transition.
Malformed, missing, stale, unauthorized, or otherwise out-of-contract input.
debugging_strategy: Freeze the first input that produces a wrong observable result.
Write the expected trace beside the observed trace.
Locate the first row where state, constraint, or output diverges.
Repair the rule or boundary responsible for that first divergence.
Rerun the failing case plus one normal, one boundary, and one rejection case.
progressive_hints: Label the input and promised output before naming any tool or syntax.
Separate current_state from next_state and write the validity predicate.
Apply this rule, then trace the boundary: External text and device values require explicit type, absence, and range checks before application logic uses them.

lessons.title: Functions, arrays, and immutable updates
lessons.goal: Model, apply, trace, and defend Functions, arrays, and immutable updates within a native-feeling cross-platform experience.
lessons.learning_objective: Given a normal, boundary, or invalid case, the learner will use Functions, arrays, and immutable updates to produce a valid result and explain the invariant or constraint that makes the result correct.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Functions, arrays, and immutable updates is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Pure functions and non-mutating collection operations make state transitions predictable and testable.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Functions, arrays, and immutable updates, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

content_blocks.title: See the system before the syntax
content_blocks.body: Use component trees, navigation graphs, event flows, and asynchronous timelines. Draw the boundary, label inputs and outputs, then trace one transition at a time.

outputs: A value, decision, or visible state matching the contract

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: State and event transitions is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. State records information that affects rendering, and events produce discrete transitions from one valid snapshot to another.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For State and event transitions, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

content_blocks.body: Use component trees, navigation graphs, event flows, and asynchronous timelines. Draw the boundary, label inputs and outputs, then trace one transition at a time.

outputs: A value, decision, or visible state matching the contract

Invalid input leaves the last valid state unchanged.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship

Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

project.title: JavaScript, React and React Native Foundations: React Native Mobile Application
project.real_world_context: A small team needs a native-feeling cross-platform experience that remains understandable under normal, boundary, invalid, and recovery conditions. The learner is responsible for the reasoning model and verifiable outcome.
project.problem_definition: Create a level-appropriate React Native mobile application that demonstrates all eight skills from JavaScript, React and React Native Foundations. The artifact must show how inputs become outputs, how state changes, which constraints are enforced, and how failures recover.
project.project_brief: Begin with diagrams, tables, and contracts. Build the smallest complete version, test it against the supplied case categories, record the first divergent state, repair it, and submit both the artifact and reasoning evidence.

outputs: primary task result
visible loading/empty/error or rejected state
test evidence
decision record

governing_rules: External text and device values require explicit type, absence, and range checks before application logic uses them.
Pure functions and non-mutating collection operations make state transitions predictable and testable.
A React Native component maps props and state to native-view descriptions organized as a tree.
Parents pass read-only inputs downward; children communicate events upward through explicit callback contracts.
State records information that affects rendering, and events produce discrete transitions from one valid snapshot to another.
Use portable primitives by default and isolate platform-specific behavior behind narrow, tested boundaries.
Mobile layout uses flex constraints and logical units so content adapts to screen size, density, and text scale.
Separate features, shared components, and services; use logs, inspector state, and minimal reproduction to locate failures.

constraints: Use only the languages, components, or structural interactions supported by the target application environment.
Do not hide invalid input, unavailable data, or failure behind a successful-looking state.
Keep current valid state recoverable until a candidate transition passes validation.
Do not embed secrets, real credentials, personal data, or private endpoints.
Make all important output and error states accessible and testable.
Record assumptions and unsupported cases explicitly.
The submitted result must be reproducible from the included instructions.

test_cases.condition: second valid input with different data

maximum documented size
duplicate or retry
out-of-order or stale result
malformed or unauthorized input
debugging_checklist: Freeze a reproducible failing input.
Compare expected and observed traces.
Find the first divergent state.
Check the constraint at that transition.
Repair cause before symptoms.
Rerun the failure and adjacent cases.
Confirm state recovery and accessible feedback.
Record the limitation if the case remains unsupported.
completion_checklist: All eight level skills appear in the artifact or evidence.
The input-output contract is complete.
The structural model matches the implementation or decision flow.
All eight required test categories have evidence.
The rubric self-score totals 100 possible points.
No secret, real credential, or sensitive personal data is included.
Submission instructions reproduce the result.
Reflection names one failure, repair, and justified improvement.
submission_requirements: README with setup or review instructions

rubric.evidence: inputs, outputs, constraints, diagram, and milestones
mandatory behavior matches the project contract
clear responsibilities, transitions, and dependency boundaries
normal, boundary, invalid, repeated, and failure cases
usable states, safe handling, and recovery feedback
setup, decisions, limitations, evidence, and reproducible instructions
first divergence, repair, trade-off, and next iteration

common_failure_conditions: The result handles only one normal case.
State changes before validation.
A level skill is named but not demonstrated.
The diagram disagrees with the implemented flow.
A failed dependency leaves a false success state.
Submission evidence cannot be reproduced.
reflection_questions: Which assumption changed after the first trace?
Where did expected and observed state first diverge?
Which invariant prevented the most serious failure?
What trade-off did you make among clarity, cost, performance, accessibility, safety, or flexibility?
What evidence would you collect before a wider release?
optional_extensions: Add a second representation and compare which relationships become easier to inspect.
Add property-based or generated boundary cases without duplicating existing tests.
Measure one performance, quality, or risk indicator and justify an improvement threshold.
Design a migration or compatibility plan for one changed requirement.
project.acceptable_outcome_example: A submission may use the supplied contract and state templates, implement one complete primary journey, show all required failure states, and provide eight passing test records plus one documented limitation. The exact implementation remains the learner's work.

cheat_sheet.title: Components, Navigation, Lists and Forms — Structural Cheat Sheet
cheat_sheet.introduction: This sheet turns Components, Navigation, Lists and Forms into visible relationships. It is a reference for planning, tracing, debugging, and explaining—not a list to memorize.
cheat_sheet.why_it_matters: The level contributes directly to a React Native mobile application. Each concept helps the learner move from an ambiguous task to a contract, a representation, a verified transition, and an explainable result.

mental_model.summary: Represent the work as component trees, navigation graphs, event flows, and asynchronous timelines before translating it into implementation details.
reasoning_cycle: Model variables, state, constraints, and relationships

input_questions: What may be absent or malformed?
output_questions: What shape and state are promised?

core_concepts.title: Component composition and reusable contracts
core_concepts.rule: Reusable components expose meaningful inputs and events while hiding visual and behavioral implementation details.

core_concepts.title: Stack, tab, and modal navigation graphs
core_concepts.rule: Navigation containers encode different graph relationships; a route should have one clear purpose and typed parameters.

core_concepts.title: FlatList virtualization and stable keys
core_concepts.rule: Virtualized lists render a moving window of items, and stable unique keys preserve item identity across updates.

core_concepts.title: Controlled inputs and form state
core_concepts.rule: Controlled fields derive displayed values from state and emit changes through a single validation-aware transition path.

core_concepts.title: Validation and error recovery
core_concepts.rule: Validation maps field and cross-field constraints to specific, accessible messages without destroying the learner's entered data.

core_concepts.title: Responsive styling and safe areas
core_concepts.rule: Layouts honor available dimensions, text scale, orientation, and system insets rather than assuming fixed coordinates.

core_concepts.title: Touch interactions and feedback states
core_concepts.rule: Press, long-press, swipe, disabled, loading, and success states need distinct rules and immediate perceptible feedback.

core_concepts.title: Accessible navigation and forms
core_concepts.rule: Screen titles, focus movement, labels, hints, errors, and touch targets preserve the task for assistive technologies.

common_mistakes: Starting with syntax before defining the input-output contract.
Combining current state and a candidate update so rejection cannot be safe.
Treating an observed normal result as proof for every boundary.
Choosing a structure because it is familiar rather than because its operations match the constraints.
Ignoring empty, missing, duplicate, maximum-size, repeated, or out-of-order cases.
Hiding failures instead of representing loading, empty, rejected, and error states explicitly.
Optimizing before measuring the actual bottleneck or risk.
Explaining what the implementation does without explaining why its invariant proves correctness.

lessons.title: Component composition and reusable contracts
lessons.goal: Model, apply, trace, and defend Component composition and reusable contracts within a native-feeling cross-platform experience.
lessons.learning_objective: Given a normal, boundary, or invalid case, the learner will use Component composition and reusable contracts to produce a valid result and explain the invariant or constraint that makes the result correct.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Component composition and reusable contracts is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Reusable components expose meaningful inputs and events while hiding visual and behavioral implementation details.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Component composition and reusable contracts, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

content_blocks.title: See the system before the syntax
content_blocks.body: Use component trees, navigation graphs, event flows, and asynchronous timelines. Draw the boundary, label inputs and outputs, then trace one transition at a time.

inputs: The data or event that activates Component composition and reusable contracts
outputs: A value, decision, or visible state matching the contract
A preserved or deliberately updated next state
Evidence explaining acceptance or rejection

variables_and_state.name: candidate_input
variables_and_state.role: The untrusted or unverified incoming value

variables_and_state.name: current_state
variables_and_state.role: The last state known to satisfy all invariants

variables_and_state.name: constraint_result
variables_and_state.role: The explicit validation outcome

variables_and_state.name: next_state
variables_and_state.role: A proposed state computed without corrupting current_state

constraints: Inputs must match the declared shape and permitted boundary.
A rejected input must not corrupt the previous valid state.
The output must be representable by the current application workflow.
Every external or user-provided value is validated before use.
invariants: The governing relationship remains true: Reusable components expose meaningful inputs and events while hiding visual and behavioral implementation details.
At most one documented commit occurs for one accepted transition.
Invalid input leaves the last valid state unchanged.
step_by_step_reasoning: Restate the problem as a testable input-output contract.
List state variables and separate current state from a candidate update.
Write constraints as predicates with visible boundary choices.
Apply the structural rule for Component composition and reusable contracts.
Trace the normal case one transition at a time.
Trace an exact boundary and one invalid case.
Compare observed output and preserved invariants with the contract.
Record the first divergent state if the check fails.

worked_examples.scenario: A learner applies Component composition and reusable contracts while building a native-feeling cross-platform experience.

reasoning: Name the observable output before choosing an operation.

worked_examples.output: A valid state transition with the promised result and recorded evidence.

worked_examples.title: Boundary case: valid at the limit
worked_examples.scenario: The input is exactly at the smallest or largest documented valid boundary.
worked_examples.input: A boundary value explicitly included by the constraint.
reasoning: Write the inclusive or exclusive boundary symbolically.
Evaluate the predicate before changing state.
Apply the same rule used for ordinary valid input.
Verify that the output remains representable and accessible.
worked_examples.output: The boundary case is accepted once and produces a valid output without special hidden state.

worked_examples.title: Rejected case: preserve the invariant
worked_examples.scenario: An input violates one required relationship or arrives in an unsupported state.
worked_examples.input: An out-of-contract value paired with a previously valid state.
reasoning: Identify the failed constraint and stop before commit.
Keep the previous valid state unchanged.
Return a specific, non-sensitive explanation or recovery path.
Record the case as evidence for a regression check.
worked_examples.output: A controlled rejection, preserved prior state, and actionable feedback.

common_mistakes: Beginning implementation before defining the required output.
Changing state before the input or transition has been validated.
Memorizing the label 'Component composition and reusable contracts' without applying its governing relationship.
Testing only one convenient normal case and assuming boundaries behave identically.
edge_cases: The smallest valid input or empty valid structure, when allowed.
The largest documented input, count, depth, size, or duration.
A duplicate, repeated event, retry, or already-completed transition.
Malformed, missing, stale, unauthorized, or otherwise out-of-contract input.
debugging_strategy: Freeze the first input that produces a wrong observable result.
Write the expected trace beside the observed trace.
Locate the first row where state, constraint, or output diverges.
Repair the rule or boundary responsible for that first divergence.
Rerun the failing case plus one normal, one boundary, and one rejection case.

activities.title: Repair a violated invariant
activities.prompt: A fictional implementation of Controlled inputs and form state accepts an out-of-contract input and overwrites a valid previous state. Select the repair that validates before mutation and preserves the previous state on rejection.

options.text: Mutate first, then hide any error message.
Validate the candidate, compute a new state, commit only if valid, otherwise retain the previous state.
Delete the constraint so every input becomes valid.
Retry the same mutation until it appears to work.

activities.explanation: Validation before commit makes rejection side-effect-free and preserves the state invariant.

wrong_choice_explanations.A: Hiding evidence does not repair invalid state.
wrong_choice_explanations.C: Removing a requirement changes the problem rather than solving it.
wrong_choice_explanations.D: Repeating an invalid transition can compound the damage.

hints: Protect the previous valid state.
Separate validation from commit.
Only a validated candidate may replace current state.

lessons.title: Validation and error recovery
lessons.goal: Model, apply, trace, and defend Validation and error recovery within a native-feeling cross-platform experience.
lessons.learning_objective: Given a normal, boundary, or invalid case, the learner will use Validation and error recovery to produce a valid result and explain the invariant or constraint that makes the result correct.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Validation and error recovery is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Validation maps field and cross-field constraints to specific, accessible messages without destroying the learner's entered data.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Validation and error recovery, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

content_blocks.title: See the system before the syntax
content_blocks.body: Use component trees, navigation graphs, event flows, and asynchronous timelines. Draw the boundary, label inputs and outputs, then trace one transition at a time.

inputs: The data or event that activates Validation and error recovery
outputs: A value, decision, or visible state matching the contract
A preserved or deliberately updated next state
Evidence explaining acceptance or rejection

variables_and_state.name: candidate_input
variables_and_state.role: The untrusted or unverified incoming value

variables_and_state.name: current_state
variables_and_state.role: The last state known to satisfy all invariants

variables_and_state.name: constraint_result
variables_and_state.role: The explicit validation outcome

variables_and_state.name: next_state
variables_and_state.role: A proposed state computed without corrupting current_state

constraints: Inputs must match the declared shape and permitted boundary.
A rejected input must not corrupt the previous valid state.
The output must be representable by the current application workflow.
Every external or user-provided value is validated before use.
invariants: The governing relationship remains true: Validation maps field and cross-field constraints to specific, accessible messages without destroying the learner's entered data.
At most one documented commit occurs for one accepted transition.
Invalid input leaves the last valid state unchanged.
step_by_step_reasoning: Restate the problem as a testable input-output contract.
List state variables and separate current state from a candidate update.
Write constraints as predicates with visible boundary choices.
Apply the structural rule for Validation and error recovery.
Trace the normal case one transition at a time.
Trace an exact boundary and one invalid case.
Compare observed output and preserved invariants with the contract.
Record the first divergent state if the check fails.

project.title: Components, Navigation, Lists and Forms: React Native Mobile Application
project.real_world_context: A small team needs a native-feeling cross-platform experience that remains understandable under normal, boundary, invalid, and recovery conditions. The learner is responsible for the reasoning model and verifiable outcome.
project.problem_definition: Create a level-appropriate React Native mobile application that demonstrates all eight skills from Components, Navigation, Lists and Forms. The artifact must show how inputs become outputs, how state changes, which constraints are enforced, and how failures recover.
project.project_brief: Begin with diagrams, tables, and contracts. Build the smallest complete version, test it against the supplied case categories, record the first divergent state, repair it, and submit both the artifact and reasoning evidence.

outputs: primary task result
visible loading/empty/error or rejected state
test evidence
decision record

governing_rules: Reusable components expose meaningful inputs and events while hiding visual and behavioral implementation details.
Navigation containers encode different graph relationships; a route should have one clear purpose and typed parameters.
Virtualized lists render a moving window of items, and stable unique keys preserve item identity across updates.
Controlled fields derive displayed values from state and emit changes through a single validation-aware transition path.
Validation maps field and cross-field constraints to specific, accessible messages without destroying the learner's entered data.
Layouts honor available dimensions, text scale, orientation, and system insets rather than assuming fixed coordinates.
Press, long-press, swipe, disabled, loading, and success states need distinct rules and immediate perceptible feedback.
Screen titles, focus movement, labels, hints, errors, and touch targets preserve the task for assistive technologies.

core_concepts.title: Local state, context, and ownership
core_concepts.rule: Keep state local until multiple distant consumers need one authority; context distributes values but does not replace a state model.

core_concepts.title: Reducers and finite UI states
core_concepts.rule: A reducer maps state plus action to next state, while finite states prevent impossible loading-data-error combinations.

core_concepts.rule: Effects synchronize with external systems and must cancel subscriptions or ignore obsolete results when dependencies change.

core_concepts.title: HTTP requests and response validation
core_concepts.rule: A successful transport status is only one condition; decode and validate response structure before updating trusted state.

core_concepts.title: Caching, retries, and server state
core_concepts.rule: Server-state tools coordinate freshness, deduplication, retries, and invalidation without turning remote data into uncontrolled local copies.

core_concepts.title: Service and repository boundaries
core_concepts.rule: Network and storage details sit behind domain-oriented contracts that views can test without real infrastructure.

core_concepts.title: Authentication state and protected routes
core_concepts.rule: Authentication is an explicit state machine; route access reacts to verified identity without briefly exposing protected content.

core_concepts.title: Feature-based application architecture
core_concepts.rule: Group code by user capability and enforce dependency direction among presentation, domain, and infrastructure concerns.

common_mistakes: Starting with syntax before defining the input-output contract.
Combining current state and a candidate update so rejection cannot be safe.
Treating an observed normal result as proof for every boundary.
Choosing a structure because it is familiar rather than because its operations match the constraints.

lessons.title: Local state, context, and ownership
lessons.goal: Model, apply, trace, and defend Local state, context, and ownership within a native-feeling cross-platform experience.
lessons.learning_objective: Given a normal, boundary, or invalid case, the learner will use Local state, context, and ownership to produce a valid result and explain the invariant or constraint that makes the result correct.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Local state, context, and ownership is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Keep state local until multiple distant consumers need one authority; context distributes values but does not replace a state model.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Local state, context, and ownership, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

content_blocks.title: See the system before the syntax
content_blocks.body: Use component trees, navigation graphs, event flows, and asynchronous timelines. Draw the boundary, label inputs and outputs, then trace one transition at a time.

inputs: The data or event that activates Local state, context, and ownership
outputs: A value, decision, or visible state matching the contract
A preserved or deliberately updated next state
Evidence explaining acceptance or rejection

variables_and_state.name: candidate_input
variables_and_state.role: The untrusted or unverified incoming value

variables_and_state.name: current_state
variables_and_state.role: The last state known to satisfy all invariants

variables_and_state.name: constraint_result
variables_and_state.role: The explicit validation outcome

variables_and_state.name: next_state
variables_and_state.role: A proposed state computed without corrupting current_state

constraints: Inputs must match the declared shape and permitted boundary.

lessons.title: Effects, cleanup, and dependency reasoning
lessons.goal: Model, apply, trace, and defend Effects, cleanup, and dependency reasoning within a native-feeling cross-platform experience.
lessons.learning_objective: Given a normal, boundary, or invalid case, the learner will use Effects, cleanup, and dependency reasoning to produce a valid result and explain the invariant or constraint that makes the result correct.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Effects, cleanup, and dependency reasoning is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Effects synchronize with external systems and must cancel subscriptions or ignore obsolete results when dependencies change.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Effects, cleanup, and dependency reasoning, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

content_blocks.title: See the system before the syntax
content_blocks.body: Use component trees, navigation graphs, event flows, and asynchronous timelines. Draw the boundary, label inputs and outputs, then trace one transition at a time.

inputs: The data or event that activates Effects, cleanup, and dependency reasoning
outputs: A value, decision, or visible state matching the contract
A preserved or deliberately updated next state

project.title: State, Networking and Application Architecture: React Native Mobile Application
project.real_world_context: A small team needs a native-feeling cross-platform experience that remains understandable under normal, boundary, invalid, and recovery conditions. The learner is responsible for the reasoning model and verifiable outcome.
project.problem_definition: Create a level-appropriate React Native mobile application that demonstrates all eight skills from State, Networking and Application Architecture. The artifact must show how inputs become outputs, how state changes, which constraints are enforced, and how failures recover.
project.project_brief: Begin with diagrams, tables, and contracts. Build the smallest complete version, test it against the supplied case categories, record the first divergent state, repair it, and submit both the artifact and reasoning evidence.

outputs: primary task result
visible loading/empty/error or rejected state
test evidence
decision record

governing_rules: Keep state local until multiple distant consumers need one authority; context distributes values but does not replace a state model.
A reducer maps state plus action to next state, while finite states prevent impossible loading-data-error combinations.
Effects synchronize with external systems and must cancel subscriptions or ignore obsolete results when dependencies change.
A successful transport status is only one condition; decode and validate response structure before updating trusted state.
Server-state tools coordinate freshness, deduplication, retries, and invalidation without turning remote data into uncontrolled local copies.
Network and storage details sit behind domain-oriented contracts that views can test without real infrastructure.
Authentication is an explicit state machine; route access reacts to verified identity without briefly exposing protected content.
Group code by user capability and enforce dependency direction among presentation, domain, and infrastructure concerns.

constraints: Use only the languages, components, or structural interactions supported by the target application environment.
Do not hide invalid input, unavailable data, or failure behind a successful-looking state.
Keep current valid state recoverable until a candidate transition passes validation.
Do not embed secrets, real credentials, personal data, or private endpoints.
Make all important output and error states accessible and testable.
Record assumptions and unsupported cases explicitly.
The submitted result must be reproducible from the included instructions.

Record the limitation if the case remains unsupported.
completion_checklist: All eight level skills appear in the artifact or evidence.

All eight required test categories have evidence.

Reflection names one failure, repair, and justified improvement.

mandatory behavior matches the project contract
clear responsibilities, transitions, and dependency boundaries
normal, boundary, invalid, repeated, and failure cases
usable states, safe handling, and recovery feedback
setup, decisions, limitations, evidence, and reproducible instructions
first divergence, repair, trade-off, and next iteration

common_failure_conditions: The result handles only one normal case.
State changes before validation.
A level skill is named but not demonstrated.
The diagram disagrees with the implemented flow.
A failed dependency leaves a false success state.
Submission evidence cannot be reproduced.

optional_extensions: Add a second representation and compare which relationships become easier to inspect.
Add property-based or generated boundary cases without duplicating existing tests.
Measure one performance, quality, or risk indicator and justify an improvement threshold.
Design a migration or compatibility plan for one changed requirement.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Connectivity state and offline feedback is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. lessons.learning_objective: Given a normal, boundary, or invalid case, the learner will use Mutation queues and conflict policies to produce a valid result and explain the invariant or constraint that makes the result correct.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Mutation queues and conflict policies is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Offline writes need unique operation IDs, ordering rules, bounded retries, and deterministic merge or user-resolution behavior.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Mutation queues and conflict policies, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

project.title: Device Features, Storage, Security and Offline UX: React Native Mobile Application
project.real_world_context: A small team needs a native-feeling cross-platform experience that remains understandable under normal, boundary, invalid, and recovery conditions. The learner is responsible for the reasoning model and verifiable outcome.
project.problem_definition: Create a level-appropriate React Native mobile application that demonstrates all eight skills from Device Features, Storage, Security and Offline UX. The artifact must show how inputs become outputs, how state changes, which constraints are enforced, and how failures recover.
project.project_brief: Begin with diagrams, tables, and contracts. Build the smallest complete version, test it against the supplied case categories, record the first divergent state, repair it, and submit both the artifact and reasoning evidence.

outputs: primary task result
visible loading/empty/error or rejected state
test evidence
decision record

governing_rules: Explain the user benefit, request only the needed device capability, and provide a usable denied-permission path.
Device sessions have acquisition, active, paused, and released states; cleanup prevents privacy, battery, and memory problems.
Choose preference or database storage by data shape and evolve persistent records through tested version migrations.
Sensitive tokens belong in platform-protected storage, with short lifetime, redacted diagnostics, and explicit revocation.
Connectivity is evidence, not proof of service availability; show cached, pending, failed, and synchronized states explicitly.
Offline writes need unique operation IDs, ordering rules, bounded retries, and deterministic merge or user-resolution behavior.
Treat every deep-link parameter as untrusted, validate destination and identity state, and reject unsupported transitions.
Map local assets, device boundaries, network boundaries, entry points, abuse cases, and layered mitigations before implementation.

core_concepts.title: Crash monitoring and release health
core_concepts.rule: Symbolicated crashes, non-sensitive context, version cohorts, and service indicators reveal whether a release is safe.

core_concepts.title: Automated builds and phased rollout
core_concepts.rule: Repeatable signed builds plus staged exposure, monitoring thresholds, and rollback reduce the impact of release defects.

lessons.title: Unit, component, and device tests
lessons.goal: Model, apply, trace, and defend Unit, component, and device tests within a native-feeling cross-platform experience.
lessons.learning_objective: Given a normal, boundary, or invalid case, the learner will use Unit, component, and device tests to produce a valid result and explain the invariant or constraint that makes the result correct.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Unit, component, and device tests is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Match test scope to risk and control time, network, storage, and navigation dependencies for reproducible evidence.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Unit, component, and device tests, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

content_blocks.title: See the system before the syntax
content_blocks.body: Use component trees, navigation graphs, event flows, and asynchronous timelines. Draw the boundary, label inputs and outputs, then trace one transition at a time.

Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

content_blocks.title: Start with the relationship
content_blocks.body: Automated builds and phased rollout is easier when you stop treating it as a tool to memorize. Begin with what enters the problem, what must leave it, and what is allowed to change. Repeatable signed builds plus staged exposure, monitoring thresholds, and rollback reduce the impact of release defects.

content_blocks.title: Formal structure
content_blocks.body: Represent the task as a transition F(input, current_state) -> (output, next_state). For Automated builds and phased rollout, F is valid only when its preconditions hold, its output matches the declared shape, and every stated invariant remains true. Validation occurs before an irreversible commit.

project.title: Performance, Testing and Application Release: React Native Mobile Application
project.real_world_context: A small team needs a native-feeling cross-platform experience that remains understandable under normal, boundary, invalid, and recovery conditions. The learner is responsible for the reasoning model and verifiable outcome.
project.problem_definition: Create a level-appropriate React Native mobile application that demonstrates all eight skills from Performance, Testing and Application Release. The artifact must show how inputs become outputs, how state changes, which constraints are enforced, and how failures recover.
project.project_brief: Begin with diagrams, tables, and contracts. Build the smallest complete version, test it against the supplied case categories, record the first divergent state, repair it, and submit both the artifact and reasoning evidence.

outputs: primary task result
visible loading/empty/error or rejected state
test evidence
decision record

governing_rules: Match test scope to risk and control time, network, storage, and navigation dependencies for reproducible evidence.
Measure component commits and frame delays; memoization helps only when comparison cost is lower than avoided work.
Windowing, correctly sized assets, deferred work, and bundle analysis target the largest measured delays.
Crossing the JavaScript-native boundary has serialization and lifetime costs that need narrow interfaces and error handling.
Test screen-reader flow, focus, scaling, contrast, right-to-left layout, and locale formatting on real journeys.
Declared data use, permissions, SDK behavior, and in-app consent must describe the same actual system.
Symbolicated crashes, non-sensitive context, version cohorts, and service indicators reveal whether a release is safe.
Repeatable signed builds plus staged exposure, monitoring thresholds, and rollback reduce the impact of release defects.

starter_materials.scaffold_policy: Level 5 supplies only constraints, acceptance criteria, and review checkpoints.

mandatory_features: Demonstrate Unit, component, and device tests and cite its governing rule in the decision record.
Demonstrate Render profiling and memoization and cite its governing rule in the decision record.
Demonstrate Lists, images, and startup performance and cite its governing rule in the decision record.
Demonstrate Native bridges and failure boundaries and cite its governing rule in the decision record.
Demonstrate Accessibility and international release and cite its governing rule in the decision record.
Demonstrate Privacy declarations and store policies and cite its governing rule in the decision record.
Demonstrate Crash monitoring and release health and cite its governing rule in the decision record.
Demonstrate Automated builds and phased rollout and cite its governing rule in the decision record.
constraints: Use only the languages, components, or structural interactions supported by the target application environment.
Do not hide invalid input, unavailable data, or failure behind a successful-looking state.
Keep current valid state recoverable until a candidate transition passes validation.
Do not embed secrets, real credentials, personal data, or private endpoints.
Make all important output and error states accessible and testable.
Record assumptions and unsupported cases explicitly.
The submitted result must be reproducible from the included instructions.

test_cases.expected: one correct output and valid next state

test_cases.condition: second valid input with different data

test_cases.expected: accepted only if contract includes it

test_cases.condition: valid retry after a controlled failure

edge_cases: empty or minimum
maximum documented size
duplicate or retry
out-of-order or stale result
malformed or unauthorized input
debugging_checklist: Freeze a reproducible failing input.
Compare expected and observed traces.
Find the first divergent state.
Check the constraint at that transition.
Repair cause before symptoms.
Rerun the failure and adjacent cases.
Confirm state recovery and accessible feedback.
Record the limitation if the case remains unsupported.
completion_checklist: All eight level skills appear in the artifact or evidence.
The input-output contract is complete.
The structural model matches the implementation or decision flow.
All eight required test categories have evidence.
The rubric self-score totals 100 possible points.
No secret, real credential, or sensitive personal data is included.
Submission instructions reproduce the result.
Reflection names one failure, repair, and justified improvement.
submission_requirements: README with setup or review instructions

rubric.evidence: inputs, outputs, constraints, diagram, and milestones
mandatory behavior matches the project contract
clear responsibilities, transitions, and dependency boundaries
normal, boundary, invalid, repeated, and failure cases
usable states, safe handling, and recovery feedback
setup, decisions, limitations, evidence, and reproducible instructions
first divergence, repair, trade-off, and next iteration

common_failure_conditions: The result handles only one normal case.
State changes before validation.
A level skill is named but not demonstrated.
The diagram disagrees with the implemented flow.
A failed dependency leaves a false success state.
Submission evidence cannot be reproduced.
reflection_questions: Which assumption changed after the first trace?
Where did expected and observed state first diverge?
Which invariant prevented the most serious failure?
What trade-off did you make among clarity, cost, performance, accessibility, safety, or flexibility?
What evidence would you collect before a wider release?
optional_extensions: Add a second representation and compare which relationships become easier to inspect.
Add property-based or generated boundary cases without duplicating existing tests.
Measure one performance, quality, or risk indicator and justify an improvement threshold.
Design a migration or compatibility plan for one changed requirement.
project.acceptable_outcome_example: A submission may use the supplied contract and state templates, implement one complete primary journey, show all required failure states, and provide eight passing test records plus one documented limitation. The exact implementation remains the learner's work.

prompts.prompt: Restate the final input-output contract in one sentence.
Describe the first state where expected and observed behavior diverged.
Explain the repair and the invariant or constraint it restored.
Name one design trade-off and the evidence behind your choice.
What is the safest and most valuable next improvement?

optional_mastery_challenge.title: Optional Mastery Transfer
optional_mastery_challenge.prompt: Transfer the level's eight governing rules to a new version of a native-feeling cross-platform experience with one changed constraint, one new failure state, and one stricter evidence requirement.
required_outputs: change-impact table across all eight skills
normal, boundary, invalid, and recovery traces
